text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LA TRIBUNE
-- Rumours of cabinet reshuffle and dissolution of parliament have little impact on CAC 40, down 0.22 percent at yesterday's close.
-- Final price of Bull shares to be announced on April 22, but will fall between 34 and 39 francs each.

-- Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure says he has "no worries" about holding the 1997 budget deficit to three percent, adding that the 3.8 percent figure reported recently was only a "worst case" scenario. Another scenario assumes only 2.5 percent, he added. Says forecast of 47 billion franc social security deficit in 1997 way off the mark.
-- South Korean Prime Minister orders thorough government audit of French high-speed train project under construction in Seoul by a consortium including GEC Alsthom .
-- Societe Generale issues warrants on Accor , CLF Dexia and Generale des Eaux .
-- Algerian government plans to open stock market this year.
-- CFDT trade union says Bank of France wants to lay off about 1,000 staff.
-- Franc zone countries show average GDP growth of 1.2 percent for 1994 and almost five percent for 1995 and 1996.
LES ECHOS
-- AGF set to raise several billion francs on the financial markets as early as next week, possibly through a new sophisticated instrument akin to subordinated debt.
-- Government plans to sell off 11.5 percent of Bull for some 500 million francs.
-- Bruxelles Lambert and Credit Agricole to hold equal stakes in Lyonnaise-Suez merger.
L'AGEFI
-- Government to proceed with privatisation of Banque Hervet.
-- Outgoing chairman Jacques Calvet says he can't guarantee Peugeot will turn a profit in 1997.
LE FIGARO
-- Chirac weighs risks of dissolving parliament.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis tells parliament "the government will, if needed, take adequate measures to keep the budget deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997".
LIBERATION
-- President Jacques Chirac to decide for or against dissolving parliament this weekend and issue statement by April 24. First round could be on June 1, with a run-off on June 8.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Chirac lets speculation mount that he will either call early elections or reshuffle the cabinet to ease French transition to single currency.
